asset_groups.note: Describes sprite rules: 32 x 32 sprites, floors on their own 32 x 20 sheet, magenta treated as transparent, isometric footprint. Use the rules, not the text.

inspiration: Isometric footprint sprite: each object is a 32 by 32 sprite whose solid floor footprint sits on a 2:1 diagonal grid, with a dotted volume above it for one storey. Recreate with our own tile size and footprint; the rule is a clear diamond base plus a tall column. Ref: docs/images/stonesense-sprite-template.png and docs/guides/stonesense-art-guide.rst line 36.

Floors on their own sheet: floor tiles live on a separate 32 by 20 sheet instead of the object sheets, so ground and objects layer cleanly. Ref: docs/guides/stonesense-art-guide.rst line 21 and the floors sheet note near its end.

Sheet indexing with a hard row width: sprites are addressed by one index across a sheet with a fixed number of columns per row, which keeps atlas lookup simple. Ref: docs/images/stonesense-indexed-sprites.png.
One frame family in three weights: bold, medium and thin 56 x 36 frames share a shape, so line weight alone gives hierarchy. Ref: data/art/border-bold.png, border-medium.png, border-thin.png.
Two-colour map pins: small 16 x 24 pins in two colours mark states on the map (red and green sets). Quick to read and cheap to draw. Ref: data/art/red-pin.png and data/art/green-pin.png.
Packed glyph sheet: a 416 x 64 sheet holds a small letter set in one texture, which keeps a text UI to one draw source. Ref: data/art/curses-small-letters_top-left.png.

Layouts as text grids: a dungeon floor or crypt is written as a text grid of cells and reused as a plan (quickfort blueprints). A character plan is easy to tune and to version. Ref: data/blueprints/tombs/ (the CSV files in that folder).

briefs.label: Isometric footprint sprite kit
briefs.why: A diamond footprint with a tall column above it reads as a three-dimensional room from a flat sheet of 32 px tiles.
briefs.keep: Square tile with a clear footprint and volume outline; floors on their own sheet; one storey per sprite.
briefs.change: A different tile size and proportion; our own wall ornament; a different diagonal ratio so it is not the same grid.

briefs.label: Two-colour map pin
briefs.why: A tiny pin in two colours reads as a state marker at any zoom with almost no art.
briefs.keep: Small teardrop silhouette; two colours for two states.
briefs.change: A diamond or flag shape instead of a teardrop; a third colour for a third state; a shadow tuned to our palette.

briefs.label: Weighted frame family
briefs.why: One frame shape in three line weights gives hierarchy between windows, panels and buttons without new shapes.
briefs.keep: Same outer size for the family; bold, medium and thin weights; a window and panel variant.
briefs.change: Our own corner ornament; a different outer size; our own palette.

briefs.label: Crypt plan as a text grid
briefs.why: A whole crypt is a grid of characters that a designer can edit in a spreadsheet and that a tool can stamp into the world.
briefs.keep: Cell-per-character plan; rooms as blocks; a file per room type.
briefs.change: Our own room shapes and our own room names; our own spacing rules.
